stories.title: 'Miracle on the Mississippi': All aboard river cruise boat survive crash with tanker in New Orleans
stories.summary: A tanker in New Orleans that apparently lost its steering slammed into a docked river cruise boat with 180 people aboard Friday, the mayor said. All aboard survived after the crash prompted a massive rescue operation for passengers and crew who plunged into the Mississippi River as the ship took on water and began to topple over.

lines: Good evening. I’m Hannah Thibedeau, and this is your Palindrome News brief.
The Montreal-Trudeau International Airport says all flights to and from the U.S. have been temporarily suspended due to the FAA nationwide ground stop, The Canadian Press reports.
Ottawa, province hope ‘aggressive package’ can prevent Stellantis plant sale: Joly, Canada's National Observer reports.

Alberta’s government is asking a judge to strike down a First Nation’s constitutional challenge of its sovereignty act, arguing the law hasn’t had any impact on treaty rights, The Canadian Press reports.
A tanker in New Orleans that apparently lost its steering slammed into a docked river cruise boat with 180 people aboard Friday, the mayor said.

Microsoft said progress is being made in bringing its popular workplace software back online as a global outage enters its second day, disrupting business communications, police emergency calls, court operations and AI tools, The Canadian Press reports.

SpaceX’s attempt to recover its entire Starship back at the launch pad was thwarted when the booster fell into the Gulf of Mexico and exploded Friday, but the spacecraft still soared into orbit in its boldest test yet, The Associated Press reports.
That’s your brief. We’ll keep watching, so you don’t have to.
